metadata.title: Google Threat Intelligence - Session Assistant
metadata.description: This playbook lets analysts ask Google Threat Intelligence (GTI) questions directly from a Microsoft Sentinel incident. When an analyst adds an incident comment that starts with '#ask-gti:', the playbook sends the question and the incident context to the GTI Agentspace Session API and posts the answer back to the incident. Follow-up questions on the same incident continue the same multi-turn GTI session, which is tracked with the GTI-Session and GTI-LastProcessed incident tags. The full answer is saved as an HTML page in a private Azure Blob Storage container and shared as a time-limited, read-only SAS link in the incident comment; if saving or linking fails, the answer is posted inline instead.
prerequisites: 1. Obtain the Key Vault name and secret name where the GTI (VirusTotal) API key is stored.
a. Create a Key Vault with a unique name, or use an existing one.
b. Go to Key Vaults → <your keyvault> → Secrets → Generate/Import, and create a secret that contains the GTI API key.
c. Note the Key Vault name and the secret name; they are used as the KeyVaultName and KeyVaultSecretName parameters.
NOTE: Make sure the Permission model in the Access Configuration of the Key Vault is set to 'Azure role-based access control'.
2. Obtain the Storage Account name where the GTI answer pages will be saved.
a. Use an existing Azure Storage Account. The blob container is created automatically on first use.
b. Note the Storage Account name; it is used as the StorageAccountName parameter.
3. Obtain the Storage Account access key.
a. Go to Azure Portal → Storage Accounts → <your storage account> → Security + networking → Access keys.
b. Copy the value of key1 or key2.

c. Provide it as the StorageAccountKey parameter, preferably as a Key Vault reference in your parameters file. It is required only to generate the time-limited answer link (SAS), which does not support managed identity.
4. (Optional) Decide whether answer pages should be deleted automatically.
a. Set the BlobRetentionDays parameter to a value greater than or equal to SASExpiryDays to create a lifecycle rule on the Storage Account.
NOTE: A Storage Account has a single lifecycle policy, so providing this value replaces any existing policy. Leave it empty to keep answer pages indefinitely.
postDeployment: **a. Grant the Logic App managed identity 'Key Vault Secrets User' on the Key Vault**
1. In the Azure portal, go to the Key Vault entered as KeyVaultName.
2. In the left menu, click on Access control (IAM).
3. Click on Add, then choose Add role assignment.
4. Select Key Vault Secrets User as the role and click on next.
5. In Assign access to, select User, group, or service principal.
6. Click on Add members, type the playbook's name (e.g. GTISessionAssistant), and select it. Now click on Review + assign and then again click on Review + assign.
Reference link: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal
**b. Grant the Logic App managed identity 'Storage Blob Data Contributor' on the Storage Account**
1. In the Azure portal, go to the Storage Account entered as StorageAccountName.
2. In the left menu, click on Access control (IAM).
3. Click on Add, then choose Add role assignment.
4. Select Storage Blob Data Contributor as the role and click on next.
5. In Assign access to, select User, group, or service principal.
6. Click on Add members, type the playbook's name (e.g. GTISessionAssistant), and select it. Now click on Review + assign and then again click on Review + assign.
Reference link: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal
**c. Grant the Logic App managed identity 'Microsoft Sentinel Responder' on the Sentinel workspace**
1. In the Azure portal, go to the Log Analytics workspace on which Microsoft Sentinel is enabled.
2. In the left menu, click on Access control (IAM).
3. Click on Add, then choose Add role assignment.
4. Select Microsoft Sentinel Responder as the role and click on next.
5. In Assign access to, select User, group, or service principal.
6. Click on Add members, type the playbook's name (e.g. GTISessionAssistant), and select it. Now click on Review + assign and then again click on Review + assign.
Reference link: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal
**d. Create an Automation Rule to trigger the playbook**
1. In Microsoft Sentinel, go to Automation.
2. Click on Create -> Automation rule.
3. Give the rule a name, e.g. Trigger GTI Session Assistant on Comment.
4. Under Trigger, select When incident is updated.
5. Click Add condition, set it to Updated field -> Comments and value Added, so the rule only fires when a new comment is added to the incident.
6. Under Actions, select Run playbook and choose Google Threat Intelligence - Session Assistant.
7. Set the rule order, ensure it's enabled, and click Apply.
**e. Verify API connections**
The azuresentinel, keyvault and azureblob connections use the playbook's managed identity and the azureblobkey connection uses the supplied StorageAccountKey, so no interactive sign-in is needed.
1. Go to your logic app → API connections and open each connection.
2. If a connection shows as unauthorized, click Edit API connection, then Save, and re-check the role assignments above.
**f. Ask GTI a question**
1. Open an incident in Microsoft Sentinel and add a comment in the form '#ask-gti: <your question>'.
2. The answer is posted back as an incident comment. Follow-up questions on the same incident continue the same GTI session.
NOTE: The answer link is a bearer token; anyone with the URL can view that page until it expires (SASExpiryDays, default 30 days). Do not set the expiry longer than necessary.

releaseNotes.title: Initial version
notes: Ask Google Threat Intelligence questions from a Microsoft Sentinel incident comment using '#ask-gti:'.
Multi-turn GTI sessions are kept per incident using incident tags, and expired sessions are restarted automatically.
Answers are saved as an HTML page in Blob Storage and shared as a time-limited SAS link, with an inline fallback if saving or linking fails.

metadata.description: Name for this playbook (Logic App) as it will appear in Azure. Optional - defaults to GTISessionAssistant.
Name of your existing Azure Key Vault that holds the GTI (VirusTotal) API key. Required - this playbook cannot create a Key Vault for you.

Name of the secret inside that Key Vault which contains the GTI (VirusTotal) API key value. Required - a value must be provided. The field is pre-filled with the suggested name GTIApiKey; keep it or enter the actual secret name.
Name of your existing Azure Storage account where GTI answer pages will be saved. Required - enter the real storage account name; there is no default.

Name of the private blob container that will hold the GTI answer pages. Required - a value must be provided. The field is pre-filled with the suggested name gti-session-answers; keep it or enter your own (3-63 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens). The container is created automatically if it does not already exist.

How many days each answer shareable link stays valid before it expires. Required - a value must be provided (1-365). The field is pre-filled with the suggested value 30. The link needs no sign-in to view, so keep this as short as your organization risk tolerance allows.

Optional. Number of days after creation (whole number, 1 or more) that each answer page is permanently deleted from the container via a storage lifecycle management rule. Leave EMPTY (default) to keep answer pages indefinitely and not create any rule. Must be greater than or equal to SASExpiryDays (deployment fails otherwise), because deleting a page before its link expires would break the link; a value one day longer (for example 31) is recommended. WARNING: a storage account has a single lifecycle policy and providing a value replaces it, so if the account already has lifecycle rules you need to keep, leave this empty and add the rule manually. Azure evaluates lifecycle rules about once a day, so deletion can lag by up to 24 hours.

Access key for the storage account named in StorageAccountName. Required - needed only to generate the time-limited answer link (SAS), since that operation does not support managed-identity authentication. Supply this via a Key Vault reference in your parameters file; never enter it directly or as plain text.

@{concat('

GTI Session Assistant — Error

Question: ', variables('AnalystQuestion'), '

Details: Could not get a response from GTI. ', variables('ErrorMessage'), if(equals(outputs('Compose_GTI_Agent_Error_Description'), ''), if(variables('GTICallFailed'), '', 'The GTI agent accepted the request but ended without producing an answer.'), concat('GTI agent error: ', outputs('Compose_GTI_Agent_Error_Description'))), '

This is usually transient — post your question again with the #ask-gti: prefix to retry.

')}
